chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When you mix with people, if you are able to have your hand be the higher (more giving) over them, then do so.

key_terms.خَالَطْتَ: to mix or associate with others

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to have the 'higher hand' in social relations according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) advises that in social interactions, one should strive to be the more generous party, choosing to be the 'higher hand' in terms of benevolence if capacity allows. This concept of 'yad al-ulya' (the upper hand) is rooted in the Prophetic tradition of prioritizing giving over receiving, fostering humility and strengthening communal bonds. It reflects the Shia emphasis on ethical conduct (akhlaq) as a means of spiritual elevation and social harmony.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who inter-mingles (with others), so if he has the capacity that his hand can happen to be the higher (more giving than receiving), then he should do so’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja’far who has said the following: “
If in your association with people you can maintain the upper hand (be more beneficial), you should do so.”
